question.text:
Consider the system of equations
\(\begin{array}{cc}
x+y+z & =0 \\
\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma z & =0 \\
\alpha^{2} x+\beta^{2} y+\gamma^{2} z & =0
\end{array}\)
Then the system of equations has

options.text: a unique solution for all values of $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$.
infinite number of solutions, if any two of $\alpha, \bar{\beta},$ yare equal.
a unique solution, if $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are distinct.
more than one, but finite number of solutions depending on values of $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$

solution.text:
Given system of equations is $x+y+z=0$
$\begin{array}{l}
\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma z=0 \\
\alpha^{2} x+\beta^{2} y+\gamma^{2} z=0
\end{array}$
The coefficient matrix, $A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 1 & 1 \\ \alpha & \beta & \gamma \\ \alpha^{2} & \beta^{2} & \gamma^{2}\end{array}\right]$
Now, $|A|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 1 & 1 \\ \alpha & \beta & \gamma \\ \alpha^{2} & \beta^{2} & \gamma^{2}\end{array}\right|=(\alpha-\beta)(\beta-\gamma)(\gamma-\alpha)$
(i) The system of equations has a unique solution, if $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are distinct
i.e. $|A| \neq 0$
(ii) The system of equations has infinite number of solutions, if any two of $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ ar equal.
i.e. $|A|=0$
